original_question: Fix 0 <= rho <= 1. Among all partitions of R^n into q parts of equal Gaussian measure, where 3 <= q <= n+1, is the maximum noise stability at rho achieved by a standard simplex partition, and for -1 <= rho <= 0 does the standard simplex partition minimize the noise stability?
target_in_paper: The open problem labeled “Standard Simplex Conjecture” in arXiv:1204.6447, in the precise formal version given as Conjecture 1 in Heilman’s restatement of the Isaksson–Mossel conjecture.
correct_elements: Your draft captures the right conjecture and most of its mathematical core: the ambient space is R^n, the number of parts satisfies 3 ≤ q ≤ n+1, the positive-correlation side asks for maximal Gaussian noise stability under equal Gaussian measures, the candidate extremizer is the standard simplex partition, and the negative-correlation side asks for the opposite extremum.
missing_details: The paper’s formal setup uses n ≥ 2 and q (written k in the paper) an integer with 3 ≤ q ≤ n+1.
The partition must be measurable and is understood modulo Gaussian-null overlaps: ⋃_{i=1}^q A_i = R^n and γ_n(A_i ∩ A_j) = 0 for i ≠ j.
The Gaussian measure must be specified explicitly as the standard Gaussian measure γ_n on R^n.
The noise stability functional must be defined, either as J(A_1,...,A_q) = Σ_i ∫ 1_{A_i} T_ρ(1_{A_i}) dγ_n or equivalently via ρ-correlated Gaussian vectors.
The Ornstein–Uhlenbeck/noise operator must be defined: T_ρ f(x) = ∫ f(ρx + √(1-ρ^2) y) dγ_n(y).

The standard simplex partition should be defined precisely as the Voronoi partition coming from the vertices of a centered regular simplex, equivalently from unit vectors with pairwise inner products -1/(q-1).
For the positive-correlation side, the official formulation is nontrivial for ρ ∈ (0,1]; ρ = 0 is a trivial case.
For the negative-correlation side, the precise formal version in the source does not impose equal Gaussian measure on the parts; your draft is too restrictive there.
The paper’s terminology is “regular simplicial conical partition,” which is the formal version of your “standard simplex partition.”
If one uses the probabilistic formulation, one must specify that X,Y are jointly standard Gaussian in R^n with E[X_i Y_j] = ρ·1_{i=j}.
refined_question: Let n ≥ 2 and 3 ≤ q ≤ n+1. Let γ_n denote the standard Gaussian measure on R^n, and for ρ ∈ [-1,1] define the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck operator by T_ρ f(x) = ∫_{R^n} f(ρx + √(1-ρ^2)y) dγ_n(y). If A_1,...,A_q ⊂ R^n is a measurable partition of R^n, meaning ⋃_{i=1}^q A_i = R^n and γ_n(A_i ∩ A_j) = 0 for i ≠ j, and if S_1,...,S_q is the regular simplicial conical partition determined by the vertices z_1,...,z_q of a regular simplex centered at the origin in R^n, with S_i given by the Voronoi cell where ⟨x,z_i⟩ is maximal (up to Gaussian-null tie sets), is it true that: (i) for every ρ ∈ (0,1], among all such partitions satisfying γ_n(A_i) = 1/q for all i, the quantity J(A_1,...,A_q) = Σ_{i=1}^q ∫_{R^n} 1_{A_i}(x) T_ρ(1_{A_i})(x) dγ_n(x) is maximized by the regular simplicial conical partition; and (ii) for every ρ ∈ [-1,0), among all measurable partitions of R^n, the same quantity J is minimized by the regular simplicial conical partition?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, if X,Y are jointly standard Gaussian vectors in R^n with E[X_iY_j] = ρ·1_{i=j}, is Σ_{i=1}^q P(X ∈ A_i and Y ∈ A_i) maximized in case (i) and minimized in case (ii) by the regular simplicial conical partition?
justification: The draft is clearly targeting the Standard Simplex Conjecture. In arXiv:1204.6447 this appears only as a compressed open-problem entry, so the draft needs the formal definitions supplied by the cited source tradition and by Heilman’s precise restatement: measurable Gaussian partitions, the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck operator, the objective J, and the exact definition of the simplex partition. The most important substantive correction is on the ρ < 0 side: the precise formal conjecture removes the equal-measure restriction there. Heilman’s main theorem proves the q = 3, small-positive-ρ case, confirming that this is exactly the conjecture your draft is trying to isolate.
